title: Charter amendments headed to the general election ballot
summary: On July 24, the council carried a motion, eight ayes with one excused, sending seven proposed charter amendments to voters at the next general election. One of them standardizes petition review deadlines, effective January 1, 2027. Earlier, on July 7, the council passed 9–0 a change to have the Director of Finance receive injury and damage claims starting January 1, 2028.

upcomingEvent.what: Standardized deadlines for petitions take effect

timeline.text: GREAT Committee Chair Kauanoe Batangan announced that eight proposed charter amendments, including Resolutions 26-61, FD1 and 26-88, CD1, will be on the Nov. 3 general election ballot.

source.quote: 3 general election ballot will include eight proposed amendments to the Maui County Charter.

timeline.text: A council member said they expect more storm damage in the future and supported the change.

timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

timeline.text: A deputy corporation counsel said that could make the office's attorneys witnesses in later lawsuits.
timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

timeline.text: The clerk's office proposed 45 days for a first review of petitions and 30 days to review added signatures.

timeline.text: The clerk's office proposed ending a Charter rule to print public hearing notices in a newspaper.
timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

timeline.text: The vice chair said the committee has 15 charter amendments (proposed changes to the County Charter) to consider.
timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee
